name: Lanoh
confidence_why: Known only second-hand, as quoted in another work.
catalog_citation: Dunn, Michael, Niclas Burenhult, Nicole Kruspe, Sylvia Tufvesson & Neele Becker. 2011. Aslian linguistic prehistory: a case study in computational phylogenetics. Diachronica 28(3): 291-323 (MPG PuRe open postprint), family-level stress statement carried from Diffloth 1976: 102 + p.c., with Lanoh Kertei in the sample; corroborated by Benjamin, Geoffrey. 2012. catalog_locator: Dunn et al. 2011 p. 300, section 2.4 'Cognate coding'; sample statement p. 298, section 2.3 'Language sample'; sample table (Table 1) p. 299. Benjamin 2012 p. 178, p. 179, p. 187 section 4.2.4. Burenhult & Wegener 2009 p. 283 section 1 and p. 284 section 2.
catalog_quote: Dunn et al. 2011: 300: "The primary criterion used here for identifying likely cognates targets the consonants of the last syllable of forms. ... It is a principle which can be applied unproblematically to the sample, since the final syllable in most Aslian languages always has the structure /CVC/. The reason for this criterion is that Aslian languages, like other Mon-Khmer languages, seldom have suffixes, and the end of the word is therefore usually part of the root and not affected by synchronic or diachronic morphophonemic processes. Also, the final syllable is the most informative part of a word in that it always receives stress and contains the greatest phonemic variation (Diffloth 1976: 102, p.c.)." Sample (p. 298): "We include two varieties of Semnam and one variety of Lanoh which we label Kertei (the original location of the consultant). The latter most likely corresponds to Benjamin's Yir and is not actively spoken anymore but remembered by a handful of elderly speakers." Corroborants: Benjamin 2012: 179: "This is especially true of the major (i.e., stressed, word-final) vowel systems"; Burenhult & Wegener 2009: 284 (Semnam, semn1250): "As in other Aslian languages, the full range of phonemes is only to be found in the last, stressed syllable of words."

Quote confirmed; only nit: the first clause is on p. 283 section 1, the stres…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final (major) syllable of the word; pre-final (minor/pre-) syllables are unstressed with reduced vowel contrasts (iambic sesquisyllabic pattern common to Aslian). Stated first-hand only for the Semnam variety; for Lanoh proper (Jengjeng/Yir/Air Karah) it rests on the authors' 'as in other Aslian languages' and Dunn et al.'s family-level statement (whose sample includes Lanoh Kertei).
new_statements.exceptions: None. Dunn et al. hedge 'most Aslian languages' only for the /CVC/ final-syllable shape (Southern Aslian allows CV finals), not for stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word domain ('last.. syllable of words'); based on elicited citation forms/wordlist. No phrase-level discussion. NOTE identity: the first-hand sentence is about Semnam (semn1250, ISO ssm), already catalog catalog record with this same sentence; no source describes prosody of lano1248 proper.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog lano1248 'Lanoh' (alt. Lanoh Jengjeng; ISO lnh) is split from Semnam (semn1250, ISO ssm) within a 'Lanoh-Semnam' node under Lanoh-Semnam-Temiar (Central Aslian). The only first-hand prosodic sentence found (Burenhult & Wegener 2009: 284) describes Semnam of Air Bah, which the authors, Benjamin 2012 ('Semnam dialect of Lanoh') and Ma'alip & Chong 2024 ('Lanoh Semnam') all treat as a Lanoh variety, but which is already catalog catalog record (semn1250) on this very sentence - entering lano1248 on it would count one description twice. Lanoh proper: Lanoh Yir (= Kertei) and Sabum reported extinct, Jengjeng status uncertain (Benjamin 2012: 166; Dunn et al. 2011: 300); the extant non-Semnam variety at Kampung Sungai Air Karah, Lenggong, has only the loanword study Ma'alip & Chong 2024, silent on stress. Note also Glottolog's separate 'Lanoh Kobak' (lano1245) is a Temiar dialect, not this language.

sources.note: p. 284: 'As in other Aslian languages, the full range of phonemes is only to be found in the last, stressed syllable of words.' p. 288: contrastive length, nasality and diphthongization apply only to the nucleus of the last syllable; pre-final syllables have a restricted vowel set / excrescent schwa. Describes SEMNAM (Glottolog semn1250, ISO ssm), which the authors call one of 'a cluster of Central Aslian.. varieties sometimes referred to generically as Lanoh'.

sources.note: Survey. p. 178: Aslian languages retain 'typically iambic sesquisyllabic (one-and-a-half-syllable) accentual patterns'; p. 179: 'major (i.e., stressed, word-final) vowel systems'; p. 187 quotes Dunn et al. 2011:300 that the final syllable 'always receives stress'. pp. 160-161 calls Semnam 'the moribund Semnam dialect of Lanoh'; p. 166 reports Lanoh Yir and Sabum extinct, Lanoh Jengjeng status uncertain. sources.citation: Sa'adiah Ma'alip & Chong Shin. 2024. Pola fonologi kata pinjaman dari bahasa Melayu dalam bahasa Lanoh [The phonological patterns of the Malay loanwords in Lanoh language]. Akademika 94(3): 451-466. doi:10.17576/akad-2024-9403-25
sources.note: Nothing. Only linguistic study of a non-Semnam Lanoh variety (Lanoh of Kampung Sungai Air Karah, Lenggong; 450-word list, 51 Malay loans); treats segmental loan adaptation (final -N > stop, vowel lengthening + glottal stop in final open syllables, r > [y]/[ʔ]); no mention of stress (tekanan) placement. States explicitly that linguistic study of Lanoh is 'sangat terbatas' (very limited) and that no prior study of this variety exists.
